title: Tu veux être mon agent?  (Will You Be My Agent?)

segments.t: After the riding-school argument, Cecile asks Gabriel to come with her to the clinic. He takes her there by scooter the next day and waits outside while she considers the treatment proposed for the film. Hear the French first and listen for the change in her decision.
Tu vas à la clinique quand?
Demain. Pas de commentaire?
Non, je comprends pourquoi tu le fais.
C'est une super clinique. C'est Mathias qui l'a trouvée.
Tu peux m'accompagner? J'ai peur.
On verra.
Merci pour le trajet.
Ne fais pas cette tête. J'ai pris ma décision.
Tu as raison. Tout le monde le fait.
Je t'appelle après. D'accord?
D'accord. À tout à l'heure.
Bonjour. J'ai rendez-vous avec le docteur Lubek.
Gabriel? Tu es encore là?
Je ne le fais pas.
Je le savais! Tu es une grande actrice.
Gabriel, mon ange gardien, vous voulez être mon agent?
Oui, madame!
Let's take it a line at a time. After the difficult ride, Gabriel and Cecile sit together at the stables and talk about the clinic.
Tu vas à la clinique quand?
'When are you going to the clinic?' This question word for 'when' sits at the very end, which is how people really talk. She answers in one word.
Demain. Pas de commentaire?
'Tomorrow. No comment?' The first word supplies the time without repeating the whole answer. The second short question asks whether Gabriel has anything to say about her plan.
Non, je comprends pourquoi tu le fais.
'No, I understand why you're doing it.' The small word just before the last action word means 'it', the operation. It comes before the action word, not after it as in English.
C'est Mathias qui l'a trouvée.
'Mathias found it.' Literally 'it's Mathias who found it'. That shape puts the spotlight on one person, and Gabriel hears the name of his rival very clearly.
Tu peux m'accompagner? J'ai peur.
'Can you come with me? I'm scared.' To be afraid, French says 'I have fear'.
On verra.
'We'll see.' The action has a future form, but the short subject is the everyday word for 'we'. It makes a convenient answer when someone has not committed to yes.
Merci pour le trajet.
'Thanks for the lift.' The preposition after 'thanks' introduces the thing being thanked for. Here the journey was a scooter ride, and they are standing outside the clinic.
Ne fais pas cette tête.
'Don't make that face.' Cécile gives an order in the casual form, made negative.
J'ai pris ma décision.
'I've made my decision.' Literally 'I have taken my decision'. French takes a decision where English makes one.
Tu as raison. Tout le monde le fait.
'You're right. Everybody does it.' Another idea with 'to have': in French you have reason, which means you're right. He is trying hard to sound supportive.
Je t'appelle après. D'accord?
'I'll call you afterwards. Okay?' The present tense is perfectly normal for something that will happen soon.
D'accord. À tout à l'heure.
'Okay. See you later.' The second part means later on today, not some day in the future.
Bonjour. J'ai rendez-vous avec le docteur Lubek.
'Hello. I have an appointment with Doctor Lubek.' In this expression, French says 'have appointment' without an article. The doctor's name follows the small word meaning 'with'.
Gabriel? Tu es encore là?
'Gabriel? You're still here?' The small word before 'here' means 'still'. Cecile comes back outside and finds that Gabriel has waited with his scooter.
Je ne le fais pas.
'I'm not doing it.' This short line makes Cecile's decision explicit. The object meaning 'it' goes before 'do', inside the two little negative words.
Je le savais! Tu es une grande actrice.
'I knew it! You're a great actress.' The word for 'great' comes before the noun here, and it is feminine to match the actress. Then Cécile asks him something important.
Gabriel, mon ange gardien, vous voulez être mon agent?
'Gabriel, my guardian angel, will you be my agent?' Cecile now chooses polite 'you' for a playful request. They have been speaking familiarly, but she treats him as an agent she is asking to hire.
Oui, madame!
'Yes, madam!' Gabriel answers in the same polite tone. The title for a woman makes his enthusiastic yes sound like a formal acceptance. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more.
Tu vas à la clinique quand?
Demain. Pas de commentaire?
Non, je comprends pourquoi tu le fais.
C'est une super clinique. C'est Mathias qui l'a trouvée.
Tu peux m'accompagner? J'ai peur.
On verra.
Merci pour le trajet.
Ne fais pas cette tête. J'ai pris ma décision.
Tu as raison. Tout le monde le fait.
Je t'appelle après. D'accord?
D'accord. À tout à l'heure.
Bonjour. J'ai rendez-vous avec le docteur Lubek.
Gabriel? Tu es encore là?
Je ne le fais pas.
Je le savais! Tu es une grande actrice.
Gabriel, mon ange gardien, vous voulez être mon agent?
Oui, madame!
Cecile decides against the treatment, and Gabriel becomes her agent again. Listen for the requests, the thanks and the final enthusiastic yes when you hear the scene again.
Au revoir!
